title: FIFA President Infantino Confirms Iran Will Play All Three Group-Stage Matches on US Soil — Despite Sports Minister's 'Under No Circumstances' Statement
detail: FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced at the 76th FIFA Congress in Vancouver on May 1 that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup and play all three group-stage matches on US soil, directly contradicting Iran Sports Minister Ahmad Donyamali's April 30 statement that Iran 'under no circumstances' can participate. Infantino's rationale: 'We have to unite. We have to bring people together.' President Trump endorsed the decision. Iran remains in Group G with matches at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood (vs. New Zealand, June 15; vs. Belgium, June 21) and Lumen Field in Seattle (vs. Egypt, June 26). Notably, the FIFA Congress proceeded with Iran's football federation entirely absent — federation president Mehdi Taj and two senior officials had been denied entry to Canada at Toronto Pearson Airport the previous day due to alleged IRGC ties, which Canadian authorities cited under Canada's 2024 IRGC terrorist designation. The confirmation effectively overrides the Sports Ministry's political objection: under FIFA's governance framework, it is the football federation — not the government ministry — that formally decides squad submission. Infantino indicated he would meet the Iranian delegation in Zurich. The formal squad submission deadline for all 48 nations is June 1. Iran's participation crisis remains unresolved at the government level despite FIFA's confirmation.

media.caption: Infantino at the FIFA Congress in Vancouver confirms Iran will play all three World Cup matches on US soil — a direct override of the Sports Minister's 'under no circumstances' statement

title: Palestine FA Chief Refuses Handshake with Israeli Counterpart on Stage at FIFA Congress — Drops Suspension Demand at Last Minute
detail: Palestinian Football Association president Jibril Rajoub refused to shake hands with his Israeli counterpart on stage in front of all 211 FIFA member association delegates at the Vancouver Congress on May 1, creating one of the most visible diplomatic confrontations in FIFA Congress history. Rajoub had previously called for Israel's suspension from FIFA but withdrew the demand at the last minute under pressure from member associations who warned it lacked the votes to pass. Instead, the PFA proposed a monitoring mechanism for Palestinian players and equipment — a compromise that critics described as far weaker than the suspension motion the PFA had been pursuing since October 2023. The PFA is separately pursuing an appeal of FIFA's March 2026 ruling — which imposed a ~$191,000 fine on the Israel Football Association rather than suspension — to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Rajoub had additionally been denied a Canadian visa ahead of the Congress (as had the Palestinian FA's Palestinian leadership); Rajoub himself ultimately attended, but other Palestinian football officials could not. The confrontation came days after three Palestinian Football Association officials had been denied Canadian visas.

media.caption: Palestine FA president Rajoub refuses handshake with Israeli counterpart on stage at FIFA Congress in Vancouver — drops suspension demand under member association pressure

title: Houston World Cup Host Committee Formally Takes Over NRG Stadium — Pitch Installation Begins, 7 Matches to be Played June 14–July 4
detail: Houston's World Cup 2026 host committee formally took over NRG Stadium and the East Downtown Fan Festival site on May 1, marking the beginning of the final transformation phase. Commercial branding has been removed from the stadium's exterior and interior; World Cup pitch installation — to FIFA-specified hybrid grass dimensions — is underway. The venue, referred to as 'Houston Stadium' during the tournament to comply with FIFA's clean-stadium policy, will host seven matches from June 14 through July 4, making it one of the busiest US venues. Houston's climate — summer temperatures averaging 90°F with high humidity — has drawn attention from sports scientists concerned about player welfare in afternoon kickoffs. The East Downtown Fan Festival site, adjacent to the stadium, is being prepared to accommodate tens of thousands of non-ticketed fans per match day.

title: Spain Coach De La Fuente: Lamine Yamal to Be Included in World Cup Squad — Expected Fit for Final Group Match
detail: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente addressed Lamine Yamal's hamstring injury (suffered in Barcelona's late-April win over Celta Vigo) on May 1, confirming that the 17-year-old winger will be included in Spain's World Cup squad despite his club season being over. De la Fuente indicated Yamal is expected to recover in time for Spain's third and final Group H match, meaning he could potentially miss Spain's opener on June 15 and possibly the second group game, but be available for the decisive third fixture before the round of 32. Barcelona confirmed Yamal's season is over but that recovery timelines are compatible with a tournament return. Yamal was widely considered one of the most exciting attacking players in the expanded 48-team tournament and his absence from Spain's early matches would represent a significant blow to Luis de la Fuente's offensive system. Spain are in Group H alongside Morocco, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

media.caption: Spain coach De La Fuente confirms Yamal will be in the World Cup squad despite hamstring injury — expected fit for the final group stage match
